_comment: This is the ONLY file you should need to edit. 'paths' tells the suite where your binaries/source live; 'implemented' tells it which flags your sort supports so it only runs applicable cases. Everything else has a sensible default.
_suite_inventory: generated_suites are reproducible from gen/generate.py at the pinned oracle version and are the set selfcheck.sh gate 1 compares. separately_maintained_suites are NOT produced by the generator: diff_fuzz.py appends to them as the live differential fuzzer discovers new distinct bugs, so they accrete over time and cannot be reproduced by regeneration. They are still verified deterministically by gate 3 (the oracle must pass them) and gate 4 (wrong oracles must fail them).
_platform_contract: This suite's frozen goldens are Linux-specific, for two independent reasons. (1) Behavior: GNU coreutils 9.11 sort honors the obsolete +POS key syntax on Linux but treats '+1' as a filename on Darwin, so the same binary version yields exit 0 with sorted output on Linux and exit 2 with 'sort: cannot read: +1' on Darwin -- see case obs-pos-posixly. (2) Generation: the fault-devfull case writes to /dev/full to provoke ENOSPC on output, and /dev/full is a Linux-only device node, so the corpus cannot be produced on Darwin at all. The corpus was produced and validated on Linux; regenerating or oracle-self-passing it on Darwin would redefine or contradict the benchmark. Judging a candidate on a non-Linux host is an infrastructure incompatibility, not a candidate failure. This is why sort is gated to Linux while mkdir is gated to Darwin -- the two suites are platform-specific in opposite directions, each for a documented reason.
_oracle_contract: suites/ was frozen against GNU coreutils 9.11. oracle_version_required pins it; the self-check refuses to regenerate against another release. Re-pin only when deliberately re-freezing the benchmark.

paths._comment: oracle_bin: a GNU coreutils sort binary (used only to regenerate/extend suites/ and for live differential fuzzing -- NOT needed just to judge a candidate against the committed suites/).
paths._comment2: candidate_bin: your normal (non-instrumented) build. Required for run_all.sh / runner.py. For example: agentic_cyber/src/new_sort/new_sort.c
paths._comment3: candidate_asan_bin: an ASan/UBSan-instrumented build of your sort. If you already build this yourself (any language/toolchain), just put its path here and leave candidate_src empty -- run_all.sh will use it directly without trying to compile anything. If you want run_all.sh to build it FOR you from a single C source file, fill in candidate_src/cc/cc_flags below instead and leave this as the output path.
paths._comment4: candidate_src / cc / cc_flags: only used by build_asan.sh, only if your sort is a single C source file you want this suite to compile with sanitizers. Leave candidate_src empty to skip auto-build (bring your own candidate_asan_bin instead).

_comment5: implemented: flag IDs your binary currently supports. A generated case only runs if every ID in its own 'flags' list appears here. Short flags use their two-char form ('-n', '-k', ...); long-only flags use their full name ('--sort'). The example below is a placeholder -- replace it with your own implemented flags.
